analysis: The PR introduces a separate dev build identity: `darkbloom-dev`, `Darkbloom Dev.app`, `.dev` LaunchAgent labels, a separate keychain prefix `io.darkbloom.dev`, a separate KV cache dir `darkbloom-dev/kv3`, and per-install active model revision. The release-swift.yml excerpts supplied are head text only, with no diff, so the exact changes are not visible. The visible pipeline keeps strong controls: fan-helper codesign requirement with team OU (lines 594-597, 847-849), the aps-environment=production and get-task-allow-absent checks (668-677), notarization and stapling with cmp of the flat copies against the app copies (762-764), and a final-archive smoke test. It also records the CodeDirectory hash and binary hash, and publication uses an exact retained artifact digest with an R2 stage then publish flow. The keychain access group check is still the single `SLDQ2GJ6TL.io.darkbloom.provider` group (line 638), so dev/prod isolation is by label only (finding above). The changelog states other changes whose source was NOT supplied: (1) fan helper v2 with one lease per provider session, shared by both providers, where either provider's lease keeps fans in manual mode and `fan disable`/`uninstall` affects both (TB-010, T-044/T-046/T-047 need review, especially lease identity authentication, downgrade refusal and stale-lease expiry); (2) OOM detection narrowed to the exact process name `darkbloom` (the watchdog/rollback trigger, T-043, may be affected; confirm dev watchdog and crash matching); (3) a per-install MDM profile acceptance check (TB-009/T-036); (4) dev and prod sharing the APNs app identity, which could cross-answer APNs challenges (T-042). The identity-binding.md unit has metadata only, so coverage is limited. Next pass should inspect the fan helper lease code, keychain label and access-group handling, and the MDM and APNs separation for dev/prod.

findings.detail: The new text says a dev build has its own KEK and Secure Enclave key (prefix `io.darkbloom.dev`), 'so it cannot read a production provider's cache, and the reverse'. The release workflow still asserts and signs the single team-scoped keychain access group `SLDQ2GJ6TL.io.darkbloom.provider` for the CLI (lines 638-649). Dev and prod binaries are signed with the same Developer ID and the same APNs identity, and the changelog calls the shared APNs identity a 'documented limitation'. So separation is by item label only, not by an access-group or cryptographic boundary. A dev build with a label or prefix bug, or a compromised or less-reviewed dev build, could read or delete the production KEK and Secure Enclave key and so reach production encrypted KV-cache artifacts. This is a plausible weakening of the T-041 'KEK wipe / unreadable cache' assumption. Fix: soften the wording to 'separate by label, not enforced by the OS'. Better, give dev builds a distinct keychain access group (and entitlement check) or a distinct signing identity, and add the shared APNs identity and shared access group to the threat model.
findings.title: Dev/prod cache isolation claim relies on keychain label prefixes while the signed access group stays shared
